newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Envoy meets rivals in Congo conflict -UN source.
newsitem.headline: Envoy meets rivals in Congo conflict -UN source.

text.p: United Nations envoy Mohamed Sahnoun on Thursday met the chief rivals in the fighting in the Congo Republic capital Brazzaville, a U.N. source said.
"He met with both Sassou Nguesso and President (Pascal) Lissouba," the U.N. source told Reuters by telephone from Brazzaville, adding "there is no news so far" on the outcome.
Sahnoun, who later flew to neighbouring Gabon, had been expected to try to bring together the two rivals. It was not clear if he met them together or separately.

Fighting between forces supporting Lissouba and the private tribal militia loyal to Sassou, a former military ruler, has killed hundreds of people since June 5. Whole districts of the capital have been devastated.
Sahnoun came by plane from Kinshasa, capital of the neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo across the river.

The veteran Algerian diplomat had also scheduled talks with Bernard Kolelas, mayor of Brazzaville, who chairs a committee trying to broker a deal. Kolelas failed to bring Lissouba and Sassou to talks he called for Wednesday.
Gabon's President Omar Bongo, a son-in-law of Sassou and friend of Lissouba, leads a separate international mediation.
Firing was heard in Brazzaville on Wednesday night and briefly on Thursday but the city was largely calm.
In similar fighting more than 2,000 people were killed after disputed elections in 1993
The current conflict started after Lissouba's troops surrounded Sassou's home in a crackdown on private militia ahead of planned elections on July 27.
